headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: kotaemon’s broad-egress RAG stack can ingest ComfyUI outputs and secrets, while ComfyUI lacks isolation and verification boundaries.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI has no shared channel by default beyond files, and kotaemon’s web UI does not imply automatic ingestion of ComfyUI outputs. However, if the operator manually moves generated text or metadata into kotaemon, prompt injection becomes possible. The pathway is limited and not default, so low fits better than medium.
conditions: IF the operator copies ComfyUI-generated text or metadata into kotaemon inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem is used as a manual bridge, attacker-controlled content can cross agents.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste generated prompts/metadata into kotaemon without review.
Strip metadata before importing outputs.
Use a human approval step for any transferred text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, workflows, seeds, and model files locally, while kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and can call broad third-party APIs. If they share a workspace or if ComfyUI outputs are imported into kotaemon, sensitive artifacts can flow into external inference services. The interaction is plausible in default deployments, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs or workflow files are placed into kotaemon’s ./ktem_app_data or uploaded through its web UI, leakage risk increases.
IF kotaemon is configured to use OpenAI, AzureOpenAI, Cohere, Groq, or similar APIs, imported content may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive ComfyUI assets out of kotaemon uploads.
Disable external API backends in kotaemon for sensitive runs.
Use separate storage locations for each agent.
Review and redact workflows before transfer.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while kotaemon’s profile does not show filesystem write or git mutation either. The main overlap is read/import of files and API use, so direct write-write conflict is not evident. Because no shared mutable resource is documented, the conflict risk stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory outside the documented profiles, conflicts may emerge.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free writes, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid a shared writable directory.
Run each agent under a separate OS user.
Keep git repositories out of both agents’ write paths.
Use read-only mounts for shared assets.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a document/chat workflow that can render or act on imported content, while ComfyUI can generate workflows, images, and metadata that may be treated as authoritative by the downstream system. There is no built-in verification boundary in either profile, so A’s outputs can become B’s inputs with no explicit check. That makes cascading error plausible in default use.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are used as source material for kotaemon summaries or actions, errors can propagate.
IF kotaemon forwards imported claims to external APIs without verification, downstream mistakes can amplify.
mitigations: Require human review before forwarding outputs.
Separate generation from decision-making tasks.
Add a verification checklist for imported artifacts.
Log source provenance alongside each transfer.
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance enforcement.

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is offline-capable and local, but kotaemon explicitly uses broad external APIs and handles API keys plus chat transcripts. If regulated or sensitive documents are processed through kotaemon, residency and retention obligations can differ from ComfyUI’s local-only posture. The mismatch is compliance-relevant even though the exact jurisdiction is not specified.
conditions: IF regulated documents, chat transcripts, or API keys are processed in kotaemon, external-provider retention and residency rules apply.
IF the deployment requires local-only handling, kotaemon’s external API backends violate that requirement.
mitigations: Use local-only backends in kotaemon.
Do not process regulated data through external APIs.
Review retention settings for each provider.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workloads.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by data class.
